output.title: Orion OW-20 Configuration and Troubleshooting Guide

sections.heading: AP join baseline and retry tuning
key_facts: For AP join failures on 4.6, remove any RF profile override from the AP group so the controller does not emit a zero-length RF profile TLV.
On 4.7, set the AP join retry interval to 2 seconds so the controller keeps the transaction active through capability revalidation.
On 4.8, set the AP join timeout to 180 seconds when join stalls occur during the second capability exchange.
For remote APs, keep one-way latency under 80 ms on 4.7 systems and keep uplink loss below 0.5% during 4.8 join operations.

sections.heading: Controller redundancy and configuration database hygiene
key_facts: Keep the configuration database below 30,000 rows before enabling redundancy to avoid sync stalls at the 32,768-row threshold.
Remove unused AP groups, WLAN profiles, and stale guest accounts before enabling active-standby operation.
If immediate failover is required after a large configuration change, schedule a full config resync during a maintenance window.
Use redundancy force-resync only after confirming the database has been reduced and the commit queue is clear.

sections.heading: 802.11r roaming validation and load control
key_facts: For 4.9, keep controller CPU below 70% during roaming tests to reduce fast-transition key installation delays.
Lower the client accounting interval to 60 seconds on latency-sensitive SSIDs when 802.11r is enabled.
For 5.0, stagger roaming tests or reduce the client cleanup batch size so the FT flush completes within 150 ms.
Cap roam bursts below 30 clients per 10 seconds on voice-critical SSIDs until the affected release is updated.

sections.heading: RADIUS Access-Challenge attribute ordering
key_facts: On 4.9, keep Access-Challenge replies at 12 or fewer attributes to avoid loss or omission of Vendor-Specific attribute 26.
If the server must send more than 12 attributes, move Vendor-Specific attribute 26 earlier in the response order.
Prefer a policy server that sends tunneled attributes first when troubleshooting intermittent 802.1X challenge processing.
Use the vendor-first attribute order setting before retesting client authentication.

sections.heading: Guest portal sessions across failover
key_facts: During guest registration windows, keep failover inhibited so portal cookies remain pinned to the active node UUID.
For planned maintenance, set guest portal session timeout to 15 minutes before invoking failover.
If a switchover already occurred, clear the portal cookie and require the guest to reauthenticate.
Expire guest sessions before a planned redundancy failover when guest access continuity matters.

sections.heading: 5.1 RF manager and upgrade readiness
key_facts: On 5.1, disable DFS on affected radio groups if repeated DFS events stop channel updates.
Pin radios to a non-DFS channel set such as 36,40,44,48 with at least 20 MHz separation from neighboring cells.
Keep radar events below 3 per 10 minutes during peak usage if DFS must remain enabled.
Before upgrading from 4.6 to 5.0, delete unused legacy guest portal ACL objects and verify the configuration database contains only normalized entries.
